result.title: Retroactive Concept Bottleneck Models for Exemplar-Free Class-Incremental Learning
result.summary: Exemplar-free class-incremental learning (EFCIL) requires models to learn new classes sequentially without retaining training samples from previous tasks. Continual concept bottleneck models (CBMs) make their predictions interpretable by identifying visual concepts in an image and using them to score each class. However, these methods typically focus on preserving learned concepts or approximating past classes with generated features, which can leave new concepts underused in old-class predictions. We propose RetroCBM, which retains a small set of vocabulary-independent statistics relating frozen visual features to the embedding space of a pretrained vision-language model. Even after earlier training images have been discarded, we can use these statistics to supervise new concepts. To do so, we develop a retroactive regression rule that yields the same predictor for each new concept as class-balanced ridge regression on all images seen so far. We then reproject the stored statistics to recover the full-history squared classification loss and thus learn how much each new concept should contribute to old-class predictions. Since the classifier may use systematic concept errors to distinguish nearby classes, we further introduce a graph-weighted penalty on the margin shifts caused by those errors. Across six datasets, RetroCBM outperforms state-of-the-art interpretable methods in all class-incremental settings, with an 18.1\% relative gain in mean average incremental accuracy over the strongest exemplar-free baseline.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 RetroCBM，在无样本类增量学习中仅保留一组与词表无关的统计量，记录冻结视觉特征与预训练 VLM 嵌入空间之间的关系，并设计回溯回归规则使新概念获得与全历史类平衡岭回归一致的预测器，再重投影统计量恢复全历史分类损失以学习新概念对旧类预测的贡献，另加图加权惩罚抑制系统性概念误差。
AI.relevance_reason: 概念瓶颈以可解释概念作为中间决策状态，其「用少量充分统计量在不保留图像时继续监督新概念并衡量其对旧类贡献」的做法，可供核查 LVR 中视觉概念证据的保留、增量更新与贡献分配问题。
